description: SARGuardian is a four-member student team from Bangladesh combining mathematics, computing, scientific processing, design, and storytelling. Team Lead Moshiour Rahman Sarker leads Scientific Core Engine development, integration, and coordination. Sagor Chandra Modak contributes GitHub Actions and UI/UX. MD Fahim develops RiverShift. Tasmia Binte Hasan contributes storytelling and presentation. Together, we make NISAR-based surface-change insights easier to explore.
summary: SARGuardian is an interactive, NISAR-powered surface-change intelligence platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Dancing with the SARs. Users select an area of interest and observation period, discover compatible NISAR products, run automated analysis workflows, and inspect maps, measurements, acquisition dates, and processing provenance. The platform brings together four workflows: AOI-wide displacement screening, glacier movement exploration, known-place polygon analysis, and RiverShift water and land-change screening. Using NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band Level-2 GOFF, GUNW, and GCOV observations, SARGuardian makes complex radar evidence easier to explore and review. It helps researchers and decision-makers identify candidate surface changes and prioritize locations for closer investigation and field assessment.
details:
PROJECT OVERVIEW

SARGuardian is an interactive surface-change intelligence platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, responding to the challenge "Dancing with the SARs."

This is not a pre-generated demo project; it is a live, fully functional web application. Anyone, from anywhere in the world, can select any location on Earth and run their own processing, provided NISAR data is available for the selected area.


Earth's surface is constantly transformed by natural processes and human activities. Landslides, glacier movement, and changing river systems can affect ecosystems, infrastructure, water resources, and nearby communities. However, these changes can be difficult to observe consistently, especially across remote and cloud-covered regions.

SARGuardian addresses this challenge by transforming complex NASA-ISRO NISAR radar observations into interactive geospatial analysis, visual evidence, and traceable processing results.

WHAT WE DEVELOPED

We developed a web-based platform that connects an area-of-interest (AOI) selection interface, NISAR product discovery, automated scientific processing, and interactive result visualization.

Users select a location or draw an AOI, choose an observation period, discover compatible NISAR products, and submit an analysis workflow. The platform presents available maps, measurements, actual acquisition dates, processing information, and data provenance.

FOUR ANALYSIS WORKFLOWS



1. FIND DISPLACEMENTS


A target-free AOI-wide workflow that searches for candidate surface-displacement patterns without requiring a predefined target point.

It uses NISAR L-band Level-2 GOFF pixel-offset observations. Where suitable data are

available, separate GUNW interferometric phase and pairwise Line-of-Sight (LOS) diagnostics can also be examined.



2. GLACIER MOVEMENT

A glacier-focused workflow that uses the shared displacement-processing architecture to explore candidate surface-change and movement signals in glacier environments.

3. KNOWN PLACE ANALYSIS

Enables focused investigation of a selected location using two separate polygons: a Measurement Polygon and a Reference Polygon. Users can examine selected observations, measurements, and processing evidence.

Its dedicated Bhote Koshi P05023 research benchmark produced a median displacement magnitude of approximately 0.9661 metres across 292 valid pixels for the 26 July to 19 August 2026 GOFF pair, equivalent to a descriptive rate of approximately 4.03 cm/day. This is numerically close to the approximately 0.96-metre result reported by Meena (2026).

The pair covers a 24-day observation interval and ends seven days before the reported 26 August 2026 event. This is a numerical consistency comparison, not independent geophysical validation or a confirmed event prediction.

Research reference: https://doi.org/10.5194/egusphere-2026-5462

4. RIVERSHIFT

A multi-date river and surface-water change screening workflow using NISAR L-band Level-2 GCOV observations.

It identifies newly water-covered areas, persistent land-to-water transitions, and persistent water-to-land transitions. These spatial classes support further investigation of potential riverbank erosion, deposition, and land emergence.

HOW THE PLATFORM WORKS


1. The user selects an AOI and observation period.

  1. The API performs NISAR catalogue discovery through NASA CMR and ASF services.
  2. The relevant workflow checks product compatibility and available source layers.
  3. GitHub Actions coordinates the automated processing workers.
  4. The application presents maps, measurements, acquisition dates, quality information, and processing provenance


The system uses actual satellite acquisition dates. Missing observations are not fabricated and unobserved periods are not interpolated.

NASA DATA AND SCIENTIFIC APPROACH

SARGuardian uses three distinct NISAR L-band Level-2 measurement product families:

- GOFF: Geocoded Pixel Offsets.
- GUNW: Geocoded Unwrapped Interferograms.
- GCOV: Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance.

These product families provide different forms of radar evidence and are processed according to their respective scientific purposes.

TECHNOLOGY AND DEVELOPMENT

Frontend: React, TypeScript, and Vite.
Backend API: Python and FastAPI.
Authentication: Firebase Authentication.
Data and job persistence: Supabase.
Mapping and geospatial interaction: Google Maps Platform.
Scientific processing and workflow automation: Python and GitHub Actions.
Web deployment: Vercel.

GitHub is an important part of the processing architecture, not merely a code repository. It hosts the implementation and executes automated scientific workflows.

CREATIVITY AND POTENTIAL IMPACT

SARGuardian brings multiple surface-change investigations into one interactive platform. Its AOI-driven approach allows users to explore different locations and observation periods instead of relying only on fixed demonstration cases.

By making radar-derived evidence easier to explore, compare, and trace, the platform can help researchers, resource managers, and decision-makers prioritize areas for closer investigation and field assessment. Its long-term potential is to support more accessible and evidence-informed monitoring of a changing Earth.

TEAM CONTRIBUTIONS

Moshiour Rahman Sarker - Team Lead: Scientific Core Engine, processing development, project integration, coordination, and video editing. Department of Mathematics, Ananda Mohan College, Mymensingh.

Sagor Chandra Modak: Scientific Core Engine implementation through GitHub Actions, UI/UX design, and final project refinement. CSE, SUST.

MD Fahim: RiverShift development and video editing. CSE, Islamic University, Kushtia.

Tasmia Binte Hasan: Project storytelling and presentation. CSE, Islamic University, Kushtia.

AI-ASSISTED DEVELOPMENT AND MEDIA

Claude Code supported Scientific Core Engine design and architectural reasoning. OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, code analysis, debugging, and refinement. GitHub Copilot supported inline coding. ChatGPT and Google Gemini supported technical brainstorming, research synthesis, documentation, and presentation development.

Google AI Studio generated the voice-over narration. Google Flow generated illustrative video clips, and CapCut was used for video editing.

AI-assisted code and technical suggestions were reviewed, adapted, and tested by the team. AI tools did not fabricate NISAR acquisitions, radar measurements, displacement values, or scientific validation results. AI-generated video clips are illustrative media, not satellite observations or scientific evidence.

PUBLIC RESOURCES

Live application: https://sarguardian.vercel.app/

Primary public repository: https://github.com/shourov-04/SARGuardian

GitHub Actions: https://github.com/shourov-04/SARGuardian/actions

SARGuardian is intended as an interactive scientific exploration and screening platform. Its results should be interpreted in the context of the available observations, product characteristics, and processing evidence.
